sections.heading: Who should buy and who should skip
paragraphs: Buy a fries-focused air fryer if you want golden frozen or fresh-cut fries without deep frying — especially if you shake batches often and care about crisp edges.
Skip oversized dual-basket or oven combos if you only make a small snack portion and counter space is tight.
bullets: Two textures or sides → dual-basket models

sections.heading: What matters for air fryer french fries
paragraphs: Fries need hot moving air and room to dry out. Overcrowding steams them soft; shaking or tossing halfway helps browning.
Frozen fries are the easiest starting point. Fresh-cut fries usually need a light oil toss and a bit more attention to timing.
bullets: Cook in a single layer when possible
Salt after cooking for better crunch

faqs.question: What size air fryer is best for french fries?
faqs.answer: A 5–6 qt basket handles most weeknight fry portions. Choose 8 qt or DualZone models for family batches so fries are not stacked.

faqs.question: How do I get crispy air fryer fries?
faqs.answer: Avoid overcrowding, shake halfway, and use a light oil coating for fresh-cut fries. Frozen fries usually crisp well with less oil.

faqs.question: Are dual baskets better for fries?
faqs.answer: They help when you want two batch sizes, staggered timing, or fries plus another food. A strong single basket is simpler for one fry batch.

faqs.question: Can I cook fresh-cut and frozen fries the same way?
faqs.answer: Frozen fries are more forgiving. Fresh-cut fries often need drying, a light oil toss, and slightly adjusted time and temperature.
